svg.title: obj.x : the data descriptor wins before the instance dict is read
svg.desc: A flowchart of Python attribute lookup: walk the MRO, and if the name is a data descriptor with __set__ call its __get__ immediately, otherwise check the instance dict, then non-data descriptors, then plain class attributes, then __getattr__. A recursive @property is crossed out in red as a RecursionError. Beside it the three method kinds and what each receives, a diamond inheritance graph with its C3 order D B C A object, and bars showing attribute reads at 4.6, 4.4, 12.8 and 49.6 nanoseconds.
svg.text: obj.x : the data descriptor wins before the instance dict is read
step 1 happens BEFORE step 2 - that is why
...and what builds the class object itself?
three kinds of method, three things received
classmethod -> gets cls, so subclasses work
User.from_csv(row) is a classmethod for exactly that reason
C3: left to right, children before parents, and
every parent only after all of its children.
